correctness.rationale: The probability-sphere normalized complex Jacobi addition theorem gives dim H_(q,q)(C³)=(q+1)³ and K_q(z,w)=h_q P_q^(1,0)(2|<z,w>|²−1)/(q+1). Every nine-line qutrit SIC has off-diagonal squared overlap 1/4, hence G_q=h_q[(1−a_q)I_9+a_qJ_9], a_q=2(P_q(−1/2)−P_(q+1)(−1/2))/(3(q+1)). Orthogonality of (P_q−P_(q+1))/(1−x) proves the Jacobi–Legendre conversion with the correct endpoint normalization. Exact independent rational recurrence gives a0=1, a1=a2=−1/8, a3=31/256 and finite minimum −47/1024 at degree 5 for q3..19; spectral branches (1−a) mult8 and (1+8a) mult1 yield ranks 1,8,8, then9 and unique squared-condition maximum 56/25 at q3. Infinite q≥20 tail follows from |P_n(x)|≤1 by its integral representation, with |a_q|≤4/63<31/473; no finite extrapolation. q3 Gram eigenvalues 225/4 (eightfold),126 (onefold). All SIC families are covered because only overlap appears.

originality.rationale: The harmonic addition theorem, Jacobi kernels and low-degree projective SIC design identities are prior results. Distinct claim: complete degree-by-degree surjectivity from bidegree 3 onward and a uniquely optimal sharp worst all-degree squared condition number 56/25 for arbitrary qutrit SIC geometry; this is not the charged bidegree (q+3,q) problem.

value.rationale: Exact interpolation rank and a sharp condition bound are natural numerical invariants of harmonic sampling on a minimal informationally complete projective design. The theorem guarantees reconstruction at every high degree with a uniform and attained bound independent of the chosen nine-line SIC, useful for stable interpolation.

limitations: Assumes nine equiangular lines in CP², normalized probability sphere kernel and Euclidean C9; interpolation conditioning not quantum phase-retrieval conditioning.
